title: Digital Education in Medicine: A Prospective Crossover Study
summary:
This study investigates whether the use of digital simulation and decision-support applications improves clinical reasoning, diagnostic accuracy, and therefore patient safety in later everyday care. The focus is not only the comparison of different teaching formats, but the question of whether digital simulations have direct relevance for error prevention, care quality, and preparation for real patient interactions. For this purpose, students complete questionnaires before, during, and after the seminar; in addition, the results generated during the seminar are used for evaluation (e.g., scores in the learning and decision application, approaches used in digital learning applications, and safety-relevant decision parameters). The study is being conducted at the Department of Gynecology and Obstetrics (University Hospital Düsseldorf) and is led by Dr. med. Jan-Philipp Cieslik. A total of approximately 300 students will participate in the study.

Within the scope of this study, only pseudonymized data will be collected and analyzed. In addition, demographic data and data on prior clinical experience will be collected. Participation in the study will only take place after consent.
conditions: We only recruit students. We do not ask health related questions.

interventions.name: During a 90 minute seminar the cohort go through case #1 with learning modality A (e.g. "Clinic Edge") and afterwards completes case #2 with learning modality B (e.g. problem oriented tutor led seminar).
